selected_topics.lesson_subject: Preferred outbound BGP route-map selection for SLA-preferred SD-WAN peers
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: BGP neighbor has normal route-map-out and preferred-peer route-map-out-preferable; SLA/SD-WAN peer preference selects which outbound advertisement policy is applied; IPv4 and IPv6 have separate controls.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: SD-WAN health-check evaluates member; preferred role/state is reflected in neighbor selection; BGP applies preferred or normal route map to outbound NLRI; peer receives changed filtering/attributes without changing the local forwarding decision.
selected_topics.failure_class: Wrong outbound community/filter while peer health changes; preferred route map never selected because neighbor/role/health-check binding is absent or mismatched.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: Compare neighbor role/member/health-check/SLA ID, route-map definitions and BGP advertised-route/community output before and after SLA transition; inspect BGP neighbor state separately from SD-WAN SLA state.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Define both normal and preferred route maps; bind the BGP neighbor to the SD-WAN neighbor object with correct member, role, health-check and SLA ID; verify IPv4/IPv6 policy separately; refresh advertisements in a controlled window.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: Two ISP peers remain Established but the primary SLA is healthy and the branch still advertises the failover community; identify the missing preferred-peer policy binding.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiGate edge between LAN and two ISP BGP peers; parallel SLA probes feed a preferred/normal route-map selector before outbound BGP advertisements.
selected_topics.uniqueness: No prior 30-day FortiGate record contains route-map-out-preferable or SLA-selected outbound route-map behavior; prior BGP TCP-AO, conditional advertisement, BBR, route transport and multicast lessons use different mechanisms.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: Global policy package assignment: header/footer policy insertion and ADOM synchronization
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Global Database policies/objects are assigned into ADOM policy packages as ordered header/footer layers around local policies; assignment scope may be all, include or exclude selected packages, with global-object and metadata-variable options.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Create global package and header/footer rules; select ADOM/package scope; assign to ADOM; resolve global objects/meta variables; install the resulting package to managed FortiGates.
selected_topics.failure_class: Assignment appears successful but global header/footer rules are absent because stale CDB metadata remains after cloning/renaming or upgrade.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: ADOM assignment status, visible header/footer policy rows, install preview, and `diagnose cdb upgrade check invalid-global-assignment` output.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Back up FortiManager; run the targeted CDB check; reassign and verify the package; if inconsistencies remain use broader CDB checks under change control or create a fresh global package rather than cloning a damaged one.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: A global package shows assigned to an ADOM but its header rules are missing after a clone/rename; choose the least destructive evidence-led recovery.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Global Database package with header and footer layers fans into one or more ADOM policy packages, then installation to multiple managed FortiGate devices.
selected_topics.uniqueness: No historical 30-day FortiManager record covers global policy package assignment/header-footer insertion or invalid-global-assignment metadata; recent lessons concern firmware, API, template, retention and task workflows.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: Alert Explorer evidence chain: quick filters, related alerts, triggering logs and rule provenance
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Explorer combines device/time scoping, AND-composed quick filters, optional severity timeline, related-alert table and details pane exposing alert JSON, triggering logs, timeline, handler and rule provenance.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Select device/time window; apply one or more AND filters; open a related alert; inspect alert details and triggering logs; pivot to Log View or create/attach an incident or suppress according to evidence.
selected_topics.failure_class: Analyst misreads empty results caused by over-filtering or disabled timeline; alert source/target is interpreted as packet direction without checking handler group-by fields.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: Quick-filter record counts, selected device/time period, related-alert fields, alert handler/rule, raw JSON and triggering log samples.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Clear filters and widen time; explicitly enable timeline in View Options; inspect handler group-by fields and raw JSON; pivot to Log View with the alert filter before incident creation.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: An alert row is visible but the timeline is blank and the analyst cannot find matching logs; distinguish a disabled view from absent event evidence.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiAnalyzer Explorer pipeline from device/time scope through AND filters to related-alert row, details pane, triggering logs and incident action.
selected_topics.uniqueness: No 30-day FortiAnalyzer record covers Explorer quick-filter semantics or the alert-details/triggering-log provenance view; previous lessons cover alert handlers, AI triage, report datasets and log ingestion.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: FortiSwitch VXLAN interfaces: VNI-to-VLAN mapping, VTEP reachability and underlay limits
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSwitch VTEP encapsulates VLAN traffic into VXLAN UDP using a 24-bit VNI and configured remote VTEP IP; system VXLAN interface binds VNI, local VLAN, routed underlay interface and unicast/multicast mode.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Ingress frame maps to local VLAN/VNI; VTEP learns remote MAC through flooding toward remote-ip peers; packet is UDP-encapsulated across routed underlay; remote VTEP decapsulates and maps VNI to destination VLAN.
selected_topics.failure_class: Tunnel absent or remote MAC unresolved because VTEP source IP is not static/primary, remote-ip does not match peer destination, interface uses DHCP, or VLAN dependency prevents binding.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: `get system interface vxlan`, `diagnose switch vxlan mac-address list <name>`, underlay route and UDP capture; distinguish tunnel configuration from MAC learning.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Use a static primary underlay IP, match peer remote-ip values, validate VNI/VLAN mapping and underlay routing, keep unsupported PIM/IGMP snooping out of the VXLAN underlay, and resolve FortiLink VLAN dependencies before attachment.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: The VXLAN interface exists but remote MACs never appear; isolate a static-underlay or remote-IP mismatch from a VLAN mapping problem.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Two FortiSwitch VTEPs with local VLANs mapped to matching VNIs across a routed IP underlay; UDP VXLAN encapsulation and remote MAC learning shown.
selected_topics.uniqueness: No 30-day FortiSwitch lesson teaches VXLAN interface/VNI mapping; the prior EVPN multihoming lesson concerns ESI/DF control-plane behavior rather than the VXLAN tunnel data plane.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: UNII-4 5GHz channels on FortiAP G-series Single-5G profiles
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FAP G-series Single 5G platform mode exposes UNII-4 channels 169/173/177 (5.85–5.925 GHz); availability depends on country, Dedicated Scan state and radio allocation; enabling UNII-4 can remove UNII-5/6 from radio 3.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Select supported G-series model and Single 5G platform mode; evaluate Dedicated Scan; enable UNII-4 when required; select channels on radio 2; AP profile provisions the radio channel plan.
selected_topics.failure_class: Channel options absent or radio coverage changes unexpectedly due Dual 5G mode, regulatory domain, dedicated scan behavior or radio-3 band displacement.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: FortiAP profile platform mode, radio-specific channel list, country code/regulatory settings, Dedicated Scan state and AP radio operational status.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Validate model and regulatory domain first; select Single 5G; check Dedicated Scan behavior; enable UNII-4 only where permitted; review radio-3 UNII-5/6 loss before deployment.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: A G-series AP does not show channels 169/173/177 after profile deployment; identify the platform-mode and regulatory prerequisites.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiGate controller profile feeding a G-series AP with Radio 2 UNII-4 channel set and Radio 3 UNII-5/6 trade-off callout.
selected_topics.uniqueness: No 30-day FortiAP lesson covers UNII-4 channel enablement or its radio-resource trade-off; prior wireless topics cover MLO, DFS, CCA, roaming, captive portal and DHCP Option 82.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: FortiNAC Admin GUI HSTS default: browser HTTPS enforcement and certificate dependencies
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC enables HTTP Strict Transport Security for the Admin GUI by default in 9.4.5+, 7.2.4+ and 7.4.0+; the HTTPS response header instructs compliant browsers to use HTTPS for the configured max-age.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Administrator visits canonical HTTPS GUI; browser receives Strict-Transport-Security over TLS; browser caches policy; subsequent HTTP navigation is upgraded or blocked if HTTPS cannot be established.
selected_topics.failure_class: Admin access appears broken after browser caches HSTS while certificate hostname/trust or reverse-proxy TLS termination is incorrect; HTTP-only bookmarks no longer behave as expected.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: HTTPS response headers, certificate chain/hostname, browser network trace and HSTS cache state; verify the GUI is reachable over canonical HTTPS before attributing failure to FortiNAC authentication.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Use the canonical HTTPS hostname and a valid certificate; correct TLS termination and certificate SANs; avoid disabling browser security or clearing HSTS as a first-line workaround; verify release applicability.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: After upgrade, administrators can no longer reach the GUI through an HTTP bookmark but HTTPS works only with a certificate warning; identify HSTS and TLS trust as separate conditions.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Browser to FortiNAC Admin GUI over TLS with Strict-Transport-Security response and cached browser policy; certificate trust sits on the HTTPS path.
selected_topics.uniqueness: No 30-day FortiNAC lesson covers Admin GUI HSTS/browser policy; prior lessons cover RADIUS, Kerberos, profiling, portals, authentication timers and LDAP identity.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: EAP-TLS ECDSA P-384 client-certificate curve compatibility on NacOS
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: EAP-TLS TLS 1.2 certificate validation reaches CertificateVerify; NacOS must support the client's ECDSA curve. FortiNAC-F 7.6.5 GA and later supports ECDSA P-384 client certificates.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Supplicant and switch/NAS exchange EAP/RADIUS; TLS handshake negotiates; server validates certificate chain; client proves private-key possession in CertificateVerify; successful exchange yields Access-Accept and VLAN assignment.
selected_topics.failure_class: Server-side supported-curve restriction rejects ECDSA P-384 at CertificateVerify after certificate chain acceptance; RSA clients may succeed on the same port.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: RADIUS log shows `wrong curve` and fatal `illegal_parameter` at CertificateVerify; same client/port with RSA-2048 succeeds while P-384 fails; trusted CA chain is present.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Confirm the exact handshake stage and compare key types; upgrade to FortiNAC-F 7.6.5 GA or later with backup/snapshot and maintenance plan; do not rotate shared secrets or re-import an already trusted CA as a blind fix.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: After CentOS-to-NacOS migration, RSA EAP-TLS succeeds but ECDSA P-384 fails at CertificateVerify; determine whether the fault is CA trust, supplicant, switch or server curve support.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Supplicant → access switch/NAS → FortiNAC-F local RADIUS; TLS handshake phases shown with failure at CertificateVerify curve check before Access-Accept.
selected_topics.uniqueness: The 30-day FortiNAC-F EAP-TLS lesson covers OCSP-only revocation checking; this candidate isolates a different cryptographic handshake phase—supported-curve evaluation—not revocation policy.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: RADSec RADIUS accounting: TLS client trust and accounting-session transport
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator 8.0 RADIUS server accepts accounting requests over RADSec and validates that RADSec clients present certificates issued by configured Local CAs or Trusted CAs during TLS handshake.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: RADIUS client establishes TLS to FAC; FAC validates peer certificate issuer against trusted CA stores and negotiates common cipher/protocol; accounting Start/Stop/Interim-Update records are carried inside the protected connection and update session accounting.
selected_topics.failure_class: Authentication may work over one path while accounting records are absent because RADSec TLS trust, client certificate, cipher/protocol or accounting transport is not aligned.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: TLS handshake/certificate validation logs, RADSec connection state, received Accounting-Start/Interim-Update/Stop records and resulting accounting session state.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Install the correct issuing CA in Local/Trusted CA stores; verify client certificate chain and expiry; align cipher/protocol settings and RADSec listener/port; test accounting messages independently from Access-Request authentication.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: A RADSec client authenticates users but FAC has no accounting sessions; identify the separate TLS accounting-client trust and accounting-message path.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: RADIUS client with client certificate establishes TLS/RADSec to FortiAuthenticator; protected accounting messages flow into FAC accounting/session state.
selected_topics.uniqueness: No 30-day FortiAuthenticator lesson covers RADSec accounting ingestion or client-certificate trust for accounting; prior lessons cover TACACS+, SAML, RADIUS proxy, CRL and licensing.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: SCIM user/group lifecycle with Auto Provision Rules and immediate session enforcement
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: SCIM client updates users/groups/attributes; Auto Provision Rules map remote groups to FortiPAM roles/access profiles; SAML profile can bind to a SCIM profile; changed membership triggers immediate authorization reevaluation and active-session termination when access is revoked.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: IdP/SCIM client sends lifecycle update; FortiPAM syncs user/group; APL selects role; user authenticates through SAML; secret policies authorize launch; later SCIM change updates role or deauthenticates/purges user and terminates sessions/launches.
selected_topics.failure_class: SCIM user exists but has wrong access due APL/group mismatch; deprovisioning unexpectedly terminates active sessions; SAML identity and SCIM group records are not linked.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: SCIM client sync status, user/group attributes, APL match, SAML profile-to-SCIM profile binding, session list and launch termination events.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Validate SCIM client, attribute/group mapping and APL order; bind the intended SCIM profile to the SAML SSO server; test join/change/leave lifecycle with a pilot group before production.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: A user remains authenticated after being removed from a privileged SCIM group, or is purged after a harmless attribute change; inspect APL matching and live session enforcement.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Identity provider SCIM feed and SAML browser flow converge in FortiPAM; SCIM group → APL → role/secret policy; lifecycle change fans out to active login and launch-session revocation.
selected_topics.uniqueness: No 30-day FortiPAM lesson covers SCIM provisioning/deprovisioning or APL-driven immediate authorization reevaluation; recent topics concern secrets, approvals, changers and API keys.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: Device and User Risk Scoring: factor lineage and investigation prioritization
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSIEM combines asset criticality, user role/importance, incident severity, occurrence frequency and vulnerability findings into device/user risk scores surfaced in dashboards with factor drill-down.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Collected events and vulnerability/incident context are associated with CMDB assets and identities; contextual factors contribute to risk scoring; dashboard exposes score and drill-down evidence for prioritization.
selected_topics.failure_class: Analyst treats a composite risk score as proof of compromise or ignores score distortion caused by stale asset criticality, user role or entity association.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: Risk score with contributing factors, associated incidents, frequency, vulnerability findings and CMDB entity identity.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Validate asset/user identity mapping and business criticality; inspect factor drill-down and underlying incidents/vulnerabilities; use score to prioritize investigation, not as a standalone verdict.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: A low-criticality endpoint with repeated severe incidents outranks a critical server with a single event; decide what factor lineage to inspect before containment.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Event/vulnerability/incident inputs join CMDB asset and user context, flow into risk score, then dashboard factor drill-down and analyst investigation.
selected_topics.uniqueness: No 30-day FortiSIEM lesson covers composite Device/User Risk Scoring; recent lessons cover incident graphs, ML workbench, watchlists, query functions and agent monitoring.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: FIDO2 passkey authentication for FortiClient agent tunnels through SAML SSO
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiClient agent tunnel uses SAML SSO and the embedded FortiClient browser; Allow FIDO authentication enables FIDO2 passkey authentication backed by Entra ID. Windows additionally requires FIDO2 configured in the Entra enterprise application; macOS behavior differs.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Endpoint profile enables SSO and embedded browser; FortiClient starts SAML authentication; Entra ID performs FIDO2/passkey challenge; SAML assertion returns to FortiClient; IPsec/SSL agent tunnel then establishes using configured gateway parameters.
selected_topics.failure_class: FIDO option absent or rejected because SSO/embedded browser or Entra FIDO2 configuration is missing; OS-specific setting is mistaken for a universal enforcement switch.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: Endpoint profile flags, FortiClient OS/version, Entra enterprise application FIDO2 method, SAML sign-in logs and tunnel negotiation logs.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Enable Authenticate with SSO and embedded browser; configure Entra FIDO2/passkeys; on Windows also enable FIDO2 in the enterprise application; verify tunnel gateway parameters and test each OS separately.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: macOS uses passkeys but Windows still prompts for password on the same FortiSASE profile; identify the additional Windows Entra enterprise-application prerequisite.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiClient endpoint profile → embedded SAML browser → Entra ID FIDO2 challenge → SAML assertion → FortiSASE tunnel establishment.
selected_topics.uniqueness: No 30-day FortiSASE lesson covers FIDO2 authentication for agent tunnels; recent topics cover onboarding, DNS, ZTNA, tunnel timeouts and egress NAT.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: ADVPN 2.0 Dynamic BGP over loopback: direct spoke route exchange and shortcut behavior
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: BGP-on-loopback gives each spoke one iBGP session per hub; ADVPN Dynamic BGP forms a direct BGP session between spokes over a shortcut, avoiding hub route-reflector re-advertisement; ADVPN 2.0 chooses shortcuts based on healthy underlays.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Spoke advertises LAN prefixes to hub over loopback iBGP; traffic triggers shortcut; shortcut is negotiated; dynamic BGP session forms between spoke loopbacks; route exchange updates RIB; SLA changes may move user traffic before the original BGP session migrates.
selected_topics.failure_class: Shortcut carries user traffic but dynamic BGP session remains on an old shortcut until idle expiry; spoke cannot trigger shortcut because the required default route/VRF reachability is missing; health check to BGP peer loopback pins control traffic.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: BGP neighbor state, `get router info routing-table details`, recursive next-hop path, ADVPN shortcut state and per-VRF health-check state.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Advertise stable loopbacks; ensure hub default-route reachability in correct VRF; use a separate SLA target from the BGP peer address; verify underlay health and shortcut idle expiry before clearing sessions.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: A spoke's user traffic has moved to a new healthy shortcut but its dynamic BGP session still uses the old shortcut; explain the session/shortcut lifecycle and safe verification.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Hub-and-two-spoke ADVPN 2.0 overlay with stable loopbacks, initial hub sessions, direct spoke shortcut, dynamic BGP peering and SLA-controlled underlay choices.
selected_topics.uniqueness: No 30-day Secure SD-WAN record covers Dynamic BGP session formation between spoke loopbacks; recent topics cover MED, quota, FEC, shortcut hold-down, overlay templates and IPv6 segmentation.
